course_name_original: Analiza si proiectarea asistata a sistemelor mecanice
course_name_en: Aided Analysis and Design of Mechanical Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental principles of computer-aided design and the architecture of CAD/CAE systems.
Describe 2D and 3D geometric modeling methods, parametric modeling, and representations used in mechanical design.
Identify and explain the stages of the modeling and simulation process, as well as the relationship between geometric modeling, kinematic simulation, and structural analysis.
Define the basic concepts of Finite Element Analysis (FEM) and the classification of simulation techniques applied to mechanical systems.
Explain specific notions of assembly design, adaptive design, the use of component libraries, and the generation of technical documentation.
Describe the principles and applications of rapid prototyping and manufacturing technologies.
Efficiently use dedicated software packages (e.g., SolidWorks) for modeling, simulating, and analyzing mechanical systems.
Elaborate parameterized models and establish functional relationships between the components of a mechanical assembly.
Perform kinematic simulations and FEM analyses, interpreting parameters, boundary conditions, and results.
Develop alternative design solutions, optimize parameters, and evaluate constructive variants based on engineering criteria.
Generate technical documentation associated with a project (drawings, analysis reports, simulations animations).
Apply rigorous working strategies in the design and analysis of mechanical systems, respecting technical and ethical norms.
Work efficiently in multidisciplinary teams, demonstrating the ability to integrate and collaborate in the development stages of a project.
Manage tasks autonomously, demonstrating the ability to self-evaluate results and continuously improve projects.
Develop competencies through continuous documentation and appropriate use of digital resources specific to computer-aided design.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Notions and definitions. Role, purpose, importance and necessity of modeling and simulation.
Modeling Systems. General principles of modeling. Classification of modeling techniques. Stages of the modeling process.
Geometric Modeling of Mechanical Systems. Methods and techniques of geometric modeling. 2D modeling methods. 3D modeling methods. Choosing the modeling method.
Simulation of Systems. Classification of simulation techniques. Stages of simulation processes.
Assembly Design; Adaptive design; Standard component libraries - Functional design of assemblies.
Structure generation; Welded parts; Drawing generation; Rendering and animation; Dynamic simulation; Stress analysis.

Rapid Prototyping and Manufacturing. Purpose and role of rapid prototyping. Areas of use. Classification of rapid prototyping and manufacturing methods. Presentation of main RP methods. Advantages and disadvantages of RP.
Presentation of SolidWorks 2015 simulation software, operating principles, modeling principles, components. Stating different project topics.
Presentation of the mechanical system project to be studied.
Realization of the three-dimensional assembly of the designed mechanical system.
Creation of kinematic links between system components.
Running the kinematic simulation of the system with commands and motion laws.
Finite element simulation of the designed structure.
Generation of the report and interpretation of the results obtained from the simulation and analysis of the system.
teaching_methods: Learning by discovery and assisted exploration
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a course component (70%) and a project component (30%). Modelling and simulation of a mechanical system using CAD/CAE technologies and specific software is required. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the course component and the project component to pass.
